    Airtable

    Live participant data

    The tables below are read straight from the organization's Airtable base each time this page loads. Nothing is copied or cached on the server.

    Published views

    Shared straight from Airtable. Visible to everyone who opens this site.

    Workshop forms and responses

    Each folder holds the Google Form and the response sheet it feeds. Staff portal only, because the responses carry students' names.

    Every table in the base

    Read live through the Airtable API. Needs a personal access token, which stays in the browser of whoever enters it.

    Data & strategic plan

    The data library, open to our partners

    Served live from the organization's shared Drive folder. Add or update a file in Drive and it appears here.

    Shared folders

    Each folder is listed live from Drive. Add or remove a file there and it changes here.

    Empty folder box? In Drive, right-click the folder → Share → Anyone with the link → Viewer. A folder limited to your organization cannot be listed on a public page.

    Staff directory

    Everyone with an Aspire High staff account, plus anyone in the Airtable Staff table. A new colleague appears here as soon as they sign up — nobody has to edit the site.

    Staff files

    Registers and trackers

    Live Google Sheets, shown inside the staff portal. The files stay in Drive, so whoever Google lets in is who gets in — sign in with your Aspire High account to see them.

    Take attendance

    Mark today's register here and it lands in Airtable straight away, which is what feeds the attendance figures above.

    Attendance and GPA

    Read from the Students table. Whatever staff record here is exactly what the student and their parent see in their own hub — nothing more.

    Every application from the Airtable Applications table, newest first. Open one to see the full answer sheet.

    A platform for everyone

    One system, five ways in

    Everyone signs in to their own hub. Staff enter data once at the point of contact, and every dashboard reads from that same record.

    Role hubs and permissions

    Each hub is restricted to its own role, so people only ever see the records that belong to them. Sign in to open yours.

    Looker Studio

    Live program dashboards

    Reporting is built on the organization's own data sources and refreshes on its own.

    Open full report
    Grey or empty box instead of the report? Open it in Looker Studio, then Share → Manage access → Anyone with the link → Viewer, and File → Embed report → Enable embedding. Both settings are needed before a report renders inside another site.

    Add records without leaving the site

    Airtable forms for front-line staff. A submission lands straight in the base and shows up in the dashboards above.

    A one-page summary you can print or save as PDF, built from whatever the site currently shows.

    Under the hood

    Twelve linked tables, one student record

    Airtable holds the data and Looker Studio reads from it. Linked-record fields connect students to parents, tutors and sessions, so nothing is duplicated or double-counted.

    New here?

    Inspiring youth. Empowering futures.

    Free online tutoring and mentorship that helps students grow academically and personally.

    • Parents follow their own children's progress, attendance and payments
    • Students see upcoming sessions, assignments and resources
    • Tutors and mentors manage their own roster and session log
    • Staff hold the full admin view across every program
    Demo accounts

    parent@aspirehigh.test · student@aspirehigh.test · tutor@aspirehigh.test · mentor@aspirehigh.test · staff@aspirehighyouth.org

    Password for all: Aspire2026!

    Demo sign-in. This single-file version keeps accounts in your own browser only, so it is fine for showing the site but not for real student or family data. Use the Flask version for that.

    Create an account

    Pick the role that describes you. It decides which hub you land in.

    At least 8 characters.

    Already have an account?

    What happens after you sign up

    • Your password is hashed with SHA-256 and a per-account salt before it is stored
    • You land in the hub for your role, and no other role's hub is reachable
    • Staff can preview any hub for support

    Change any section here. Everything saves in this browser and the site updates straight away.

    Build 2026-09-08 If the footer of your file shows an older date, you are on an out-of-date download.
    Read this before real student records go in. In this single-file version the role check runs in the visitor’s own browser. It hides the staff portal from ordinary visitors, but anyone who knows browser developer tools can reveal it. Treat it as a demonstration and presentation site. The moment actual participant records are involved, move to the Flask version, where the check happens on the server and cannot be bypassed.

    Contact details

    Shown in the Contact section of the public portal. Without these, families have no way to reach the organization from the site.

    Accounts

    The site ships with five demonstration accounts so the hubs can be tried out. Remove them before sharing the site with anyone outside the team.

    Public application forms

    Enrollment and volunteer forms shown in Get involved. Use an Airtable form view → Share form.

    After School sign-up by grade

    One Google Form per grade, shown on the home page under Programs. Paste each grade's form link below. A grade left blank points at the first public form above instead, so families always land somewhere that works. The forms live in the Afterschool Program folder, which is listed in the staff portal under Live data → Workshop forms and responses.

    Power BI

    Paste an embed link from Power BI. File → Embed report → Website or portal gives a secure link that asks viewers to sign in. Publish to web gives a public link — quicker, but readable by anyone, so never use it for a dataset with student names.

    Staff files

    Google Sheets or Docs shown in the staff portal only. Paste the normal share link — the file stays in Drive and Google decides who can open it.

    Calendar events

    These fill the calendar on the site. A weekly event repeats every seven days until the end date. The optional link can point at a training video, a dashboard or a form.

    Google Calendar (optional second view)

    Calendar settings → Integrate calendar. The calendar must be public.

    Worth covering: ages served, cost, times, transport, what to bring.

    About page

    Team members

    Data entry forms

    Airtable form views embedded in the staff portal. In Airtable open a form view → Share form → copy the link.

    Training material

    Paste a YouTube link (or its full embed code) to add a video, or any web address to add a course. New topics appear as tabs automatically.

    Drive folders

    Each folder becomes a tab in the data library. Paste the folder link — the ID is pulled out automatically. The folder must be shared as “anyone with the link — viewer”.

    Airtable shared views

    The simplest way to put your base on the site. In Airtable open a view → Share view → Create a shareable grid view link, copy it, paste it here. No token needed, and every visitor sees it.

    Add several views at once

    One per line. Either just the link, or Label | link. Full <iframe> snippets work too — paste one table per line and every table in your base becomes a tab.

    Shared view vs token connection. A shared view is public — anyone with the site link sees those records, and Airtable itself decides what renders. The token connection below is private to your browser and drives the hub KPI numbers. Use shared views for anything you're happy to publish, and the token for anything scoped per person.

    Airtable connection

    Connect your base and the hub numbers switch from sample figures to live counts. This page only ever reads from Airtable — it never writes.

    airtable.com → account → builder hub → personal access tokens. Scopes: data.records:read and schema.bases:read. Add your base to the token.

    Open the base in a browser — the ID starts with app. Whole URL works too.

    Table names in your base

    Field names used for filtering

    Each person is matched to their records by email, so these fields must hold the same address the person signs in with.

    Before pointing this at real student records. The token is stored in this browser only — it is never written into the file and nobody else who opens the site can see it. Even so, use a read-only token limited to this one base, and test with one family first to confirm a parent account sees only their own children.

    Import a spreadsheet into Airtable

    Export a sheet from Drive as CSV (File → Download → Comma-separated values), then load it here. Each column heading must match a field name in the chosen table.

    Run Save and test connection above first so this list fills from your base.

    Rows are created in batches of 10, well inside Airtable's rate limit.

    This is the one place the site writes to Airtable. It needs the data.records:write scope on your token — without it the import stops with a clear 403 and nothing is changed. Import creates new records only; it never edits or deletes existing ones. Try one small file first, check the result in Airtable, then do the rest.

    Looker Studio dashboards

    Paste the report link. Old datastudio.google.com links work — the ID is pulled out automatically.

    Data library documents

    Give each card its own file link so visitors land on the exact document.

    Programs

    Role hubs

    One permission per line. KPIs use Label | Value per line.
